ORAL ORDER 1. Rule.
Learned APP waives service of notice of Rule on behalf of respondent-State.

2. This application is filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita for regular bail in connection with F.I.R. No. 11203030240442 of 2024, registered with Keshod Police Station,
District: Junagadh, for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2) of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, and Sections 4, 5(L), 6, 8, and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Section 67(b) of the Information Technology Act.

sentences.text: 3. Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that considering the nature of offence and role attributed to the applicant, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.

4. The learned APP appearing for the respondent State has vehemently submitted that, at the time of commission of the offence, the age of the applicant was 33 years, whereas, the age of the victim was only 17 years and 6 months and thereby, the applicant was almost double the age of the prosecutrix, at the relevant point of time.

It was also submitted that the applicant not only entered into physical relations with the prosecutrix, but, he also videographed the same and by blackmailing the prosecutrix, on the basis of such video clips, he forced her to submit herself to him.

It was,
therefore, submitted that the offences which have been charged, being serious in nature and looking to the facts as well as the allegations leveled against the applicant, no discretion is required to be exercised.

4.1 Learned Advocate, Mr. Joshi, appearing for the first informant adopted the submissions made by the learned APP and further submitted that, though, the applicant happened to be married and double the age of the prosecutrix, he compelled her to continue such illicit relations with the help of the video clip of the intimate moments with the prosecutrix recorded by him.
He also, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/20318/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined therefore, prayed to dismiss this application.

5. Heard learned advocates appearing for the parties and perused the material available on record.
From the record it appears that the investigation is over and Charge-sheet has already been filed.

It,
further, appears from the papers that the prosecutrix and the applicant knew each other and that they used to have physical relation with the consent of the prosecutrix, who was 17 years and 6 months of age, at the relevant point of time.

Though, the prosecutrix in her statement, recorded under Section 164 of the Code, has stated that the applicant physically abused her against her will and also videographed the same, the statement given by her before police is contrary to the same.
Hence, this application deserves to be allowed.

6. This court has also considered the following aspects:
(a) As per catena of decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court, there are mainly 3 factors which are required to be considered by this court i.e. prima facie case, availability of Applicant accused at the time of trial and tampering and hampering with the witnesses by the accused.
(b) That the learned Advocate for the Applicant has submitted that the Applicant Accused is not likely to flee away.
(c) That the Applicant is in custody since 23.06.2024.

In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of allegations made in the FIR and without discussing the evidence in details as well as without going into details, prima-facie,
this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion to enlarge the applicant on bail.

If accused does not possess passport,
shall file an Affidavit to that effect;
(h) shall mark presence before the concerned police station once in a month for a period of six months between 11:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.
8.
The authorities concerned shall release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.

If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/20318/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined the matter.
Bail bond to be executed before the lower court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions in accordance with law.
9. At the trial, the concerned trial Court shall not be influenced by the prima facie observations made by this Court in the present order.
